title: Bracket the two-type Gaussian funding threshold and prove the 0.0039 scaling obstruction
body:
## Mathematical result

For the two Gaussian types in ToikY’s #8072, with any nonnegative occurrence frequencies of positive total mass and a fixed integer number of rank-preserving half-splits in each type, the aggregate raw funding threshold lies strictly between **0.003898466610885757242** and **0.003898466610885757243**. The lower certificate uses 1,006 whole splits in the first type, zero in the second, and a rational 51-edge flow respecting 5r ≤ 4k. The upper certificate exhausts the integer alternatives through two exact positive row combinations. When split counts may be real, the threshold lies strictly between 0.003898466621505769638 and 0.003898466621505769639.

A separate corollary settles 0.0039 for any finite positive-scale mixture of this fixed word, including arbitrary positive rank-preserving subdivisions of paid occurrences and even with the grade restriction removed. At the target, the unsplit base word already has raw deficit greater than 1.53934254762. Homogeneity preserves its sign at every positive scale, while concavity makes subdivision increase the paid sum. A changed productive target or a physically changed paid word remains open.

## Task, credit and scope

The source is [ToikY’s #8072](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8072), head `75f7e1c44f48c43983016bcf8878c4d9e5e87c62`, including Ali Romman’s authenticated #8057 producer. [#8073](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8073) and [#8076](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8076) change ordinary or finite-resource pricing. [#8075](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8075) checks fixed-interface geometric alternatives. This refined scalar-to-moment task gives raw Gaussian feasibility and impossibility certificates. It claims no signed κ from the fractional flow. The shared historical package preflight is pinned to parent `0618e75a22cec54d1651394ef83d088551b7f026`.

## Validation and next question

Ran the standalone checker and the generic registered replay on a fresh public export with Git and CPython 3.12. Reproduce with `python3.12 -IB scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-two-type-threshold`. The checker reconstructs the public-source word and authenticates its census, prices every cut with outward intervals, checks the saved rational flow and Farkas multipliers, and rejects a changed multiplier, invalid split count, forbidden edge and mutated census. Original full-archive restoration was also run during research. The public package contains the source projection needed by this replay and retains the upstream notices. Clear1nsight used OpenAI Codex Astra and Terra for mathematical research, implementation, checking and writing.

Can the lower integer flow be assigned legal native tickets with the required ordering, source windows, precision and owned return? Until those are priced, the lower endpoint belongs to this aggregate funding model.
